semantics.summary: Records may be lost but never duplicated. Derived when no checkpoint exists or offsets auto-commit before processing.
Records are never lost but may be duplicated. The floor for checkpointed streams writing to non-transactional sinks (console, kafka, plain foreachBatch).
Duplicates are suppressed by transactional/idempotent writes (delta/iceberg micro-batch commits, batch_id dedup in foreachBatch). Not engine-claimed exactly-once.

An engine-level claim (Flink CheckpointingMode.EXACTLY_ONCE + two-phase transactional sink). Static analysis reports it as a *claim* - end-to-end truth still depends on the sink honoring transaction boundaries.
Insufficient evidence (missing source/sink/checkpoint facts) - never fabricate a guarantee.

rules.summary: Without a checkpoint, a restart cannot recover progress - records may be lost.
A non-replayable source (socket, custom non-replayable) cannot re-read lost input, capping recovery at at-least-once even with a transactional sink.
Spark SS kafka sinks write at-least-once; exactly-once to kafka requires consumer-side dedup not visible statically.
Flink EXACTLY_ONCE checkpointing only yields end-to-end exactly-once when the sink participates in the two-phase commit protocol.
